key_insight: Leakage-controlled feature engineering mattered more than classifier choice: the expert-reconstructed EEG feature set performed best overall for ADHD classification in children.
clinical_relevance: For EEG-based ADHD research, results should be interpreted cautiously and validated externally before any clinical use, because performance was modest and sensitive to preprocessing choices.
method: 77 children (45 ADHD, 32 controls) with 1,185 gamma-free EEG features
Compared expert-reconstructed, LLM-guided, and full-space feature strategies
Used nested leave-one-subject-out validation and repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation with four classifiers (SVM, GMM, RF, XGBoost)
evidence_signal: RF with the expert feature set reached 62.8% mean accuracy and 62.3% balanced accuracy across 100 repeated CV runs, while LOOCV gave 71.4% accuracy; GMM/expert had the highest AUC-ROC at 0.699.
watch_item: An artifact-filtering threshold changed results substantially, suggesting performance may depend on preprocessing and reduced epoch counts rather than robust signal alone.
paper_title: Feature-Engineering Strategies for EEG-Based ADHD Classification in Children: A Controlled Benchmark of Expert, LLM-Guided and Full-Space Comparators
